units.title: Hello
units.topic: Daily life: interaction, polite behaviour (交往)
notes: Chinese has two words for "you": 你 nǐ, for friends and people your own age, and 您 nín, a polite "you" for elders, teachers and people you want to show respect to. 您好 is a respectful hello.
In class, students greet their teacher together with 老师好! ("hello, teacher"). Among friends a greeting is often simply the other person's name.

dialogue.en: Sorry, I'm not a student, I'm a teacher.
dialogue.text: 对不起，我不是学生，我是老师。

units.title: About me
units.topic: Basic information: personal information (个人信息)
notes: In a Chinese name the family name comes first. In 王丽 Wáng Lì, 王 is the family name and 丽 the given name. Most family names are a single character.
People are often addressed by family name and title, like 李老师 ("Teacher Li"), rather than by their given name.
你几岁？ expects a small number, so it is how you ask a child's age. With adults, 你多大？ is more usual, and elders are asked more politely still.

dialogue.en: Yes, she's our teacher. She's Teacher Li.
dialogue.text: 是，她是我们老师，她叫李老师。

dialogue.en: Nice to meet you too! Where are you from?
dialogue.text: 我也很高兴！你是哪国人？
我是英国人。你是中国人吗？

dialogue.en: Teacher Li, is this your child?
dialogue.text: 李老师，这是您的孩子吗？

dialogue.en: How old are you, little one?
He's little. And you? How old are you this year?
dialogue.text: 他很小。你呢？你今年多大？

builds.en: How old are you? (to a child)

units.title: Numbers and dates
units.topic: Basic information: event information (事件信息)
notes: Before a measure word, "two" is 两 liǎng, not 二 èr: 两个人, two people. 二 is for counting and for numbers like 十二.
Dates run from big to small: year, month, day. Years are read digit by digit (二零二六年), and in speech the day of the month is 号.

dialogue.en: How many of you are there?
One, two, three, four. There are four of us.
He's seven. His friend is nine.

builds.en: How many of you are there?

dialogue.en: Today is Saturday, tomorrow is Sunday.
dialogue.text: 今天星期六，明天星期天。

dialogue.en: Last year was 2025, next year is 2027.
dialogue.text: 去年是二零二五年，明年是二零二七年。

units.title: Family
units.topic: Basic information: personal information, family and friends (个人信息)
notes: Chinese names older and younger siblings differently: 哥哥 and 姐姐 are older brother and sister, 弟弟 and 妹妹 younger ones.
个 is the everyday measure word, but animals take 只: 一只猫, a cat.

dialogue.en: How many people are in your family?
Dad, Mum, my older brother, my younger sister and me.
dialogue.text: 爸爸，妈妈，哥哥，妹妹和我。

dialogue.en: Do you have an older sister?
I don't have an older sister. And you?
I have a younger brother, and no older brother.
dialogue.text: 我有一个弟弟，没有哥哥。

dialogue.en: How old is your younger brother?

builds.en: There are five people in my family.
I don't have an older sister.
Do you have a younger brother?

dialogue.en: Yes. This is my son, and that's my daughter.
dialogue.text: 是。这是我的儿子，那是我的女儿。

dialogue.en: Does your son have a girlfriend?
He does, he loves her very much.
And your daughter? Does she have a boyfriend?
dialogue.text: 你的女儿呢？她有男朋友吗？

dialogue.en: She's eight! She loves our cat.
dialogue.text: 她八岁！她爱我们家的猫。

dialogue.en: We have a dog. It's called Dahei.
dialogue.text: 我家有一只狗，它叫大黑。

units.title: Eating
units.topic: Daily life: food and drink (饮食)
notes: Rice (米饭) is the everyday staple in the south of China; noodles (面条儿) and steamed buns (包子) more so in the north.
The 儿 at the end of 面条儿 is erhua, typical of Beijing speech; many speakers simply say 面条.

dialogue.en: What would you like to eat?
What would you like to drink? Tea?
No, I don't drink tea. I'll have water.
I'll have milk. I'm really hungry!

builds.en: What would you like to drink?

dialogue.en: What do you have for breakfast?
I have eggs and bread, and drink milk.
dialogue.text: 我吃鸡蛋和面包，喝牛奶。

dialogue.en: I have steamed buns. They're delicious!
dialogue.text: 我早饭吃包子。包子很好吃！

dialogue.en: Rice and vegetables. For dinner I have noodles.
dialogue.text: 米饭和菜。晚饭我吃面条儿。

builds.en: I have steamed buns for breakfast.

units.title: Shopping
notes: Prices are in 元 yuán on labels, but in speech people say 块 kuài: 五块 is five yuan.
太…了 means "too…": 太贵了, too expensive. The 了 marks it as a reaction to how things are.

dialogue.en: Hello! How much are the apples?
It's not expensive, it's cheap! How many would you like?
I'll take two. What else do you sell?
I also sell milk and bread.
You look pretty in this one.
What about that one? That one's nice too.
Things in this shop are expensive.
Things at the supermarket are cheap.

builds.en: Things at the supermarket are cheap.

units.title: Getting around
notes: To ask a stranger anything, start with 请问, "may I ask": it is the polite way in.
坐 means "to sit", and it is also how you take a vehicle: 坐出租车, 坐火车, 坐飞机.

dialogue.en: How are you getting to Shanghai tomorrow?
He doesn't drive. We take taxis.
dialogue.text: 他不开车。我们坐出租车。

dialogue.en: Excuse me, is this a taxi?
Yes, this is my car. Please, have a seat!
We're going to the supermarket, is that all right?

units.title: Weather and time
units.topic: Basic information: environment, weather (环境信息)
notes: 有点儿 means "a bit", and usually a bit too much of something unwelcome: 有点儿冷, a bit cold.
Clock times: 点 is o'clock, 分 minutes and 半 half past: 九点半 is half past nine.

dialogue.en: A bit cold. It's been really hot these last few days!
I don't like rain. I like snow!
I like snow too, it's beautiful.
What time do you have breakfast?
You're early! I eat at ten past eight.
Are you at home in the morning?
In the morning, yes; at noon and in the afternoon, no.
dialogue.text: 上午在家，中午和下午不在。

dialogue.en: In the evening I'm at home.

builds.en: Are you at home in the morning?
